Table 2 (Appendix A) states 50 samples but SRs 15.3/23.1/28.8 equal 8/52, 12/52, 15/52; with n=50 rates must be multiples of 2.0. Pilot n inconsistent (our arithmetic; also found by son55).
range(501, 1000) yields 499 seeds, versus the stated 500 trajectories (our arithmetic; found by both seats).

Fig 5a shares are of each method's own failures. Taking failure = non-success, approximate per-task invalid-loop rates are ReAct 0.127*0.766=9.7% and ASH 0.104*0.698=7.3%; the share comparison hides different failure counts (our approximate arithmetic, failure definition not stated by authors).
Table 1 code-davinci-002 SR difference 30.2-23.4=6.8 pt (29% relative) contradicts abstract 6.2%.

Binomial SE of an SR near 0.25-0.30 at n~500 is about 2 pt; a 6.8 pt gap is likely but not demonstrably beyond noise for a single greedy run; the 4.0 pt DIRECT+ASH vs ReAct gap and 2.3 pt invalid-share gap are not (our arithmetic; also son55).

ASH's 500 sampled sessions are not stated to be WebShop's fixed 500-instruction test split (A18 vs W01/W02); published ReAct 40.0 SR (R01) used a different backbone, observation mode and the standard split. 'Outperforms previous state of the art' therefore holds only relative to the in-house ReAct re-implementation (A17) under ASH's harness.

gap.closest_adjacent: ReAct on WebShop (reasoning over noisy observations, hand-trimmed exemplars) and WebShop simple mode (rule-based observation simplification).

gap.stakes: Context exhaustion, invalid-action loops, premature purchase of partly matching items.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Interactive WebShop simulator with programmatic reward (W05); one simulated site, text-only, no unseen environment -> not transfer (EVIDENCE.md rules 1-2). Both seats agree.
assessment.author_claim_kept: ASH outperforms prior SOTA prompting (ReAct) on WebShop; helps long trajectories; reduces hallucinated invalid actions; mitigates need for explicit reasoning; broad applicability.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In the authors' single greedy run on ~500 randomly sampled WebShop text_rich sessions (not stated to be the standard test split), replacing raw observations with per-step LLM-condensed observations raised SR from 23.4 to 30.2 (code-davinci-002) and 3.0 to 12.6 (gpt-3.5-turbo, where raw ReAct overflows 4k), against the authors' own ReAct re-implementation.
cannot_say: gain exceeds run noise or a rule-based condensation baseline
summarisation rather than shortening/hints causes the gain
works beyond WebShop or in real browsers

G.reason: Specific bottleneck located: long/noisy raw WebShop observations degrade a prompted actor (4k overflow on gpt-3.5, ReAct 7.4 avg beyond 11 realised steps, repeated invalid actions). Lineage now verified against shared originals: ReAct itself frames WebShop observations as noisy and handles them by in-actor reasoning (R02, R03), with exemplar results pages trimmed to 3 of 10 items (R04, W03); ASH's residue (explicit, goal/action-conditioned observation encoding separate from acting) is correctly placed (A13, A14). Not 4: adjacent cheap condensers in the same environment (WebShop simple mode W04, ReAct-style top-k trimming) are not compared, so the residual gap relative to rule-based condensation is unbounded; overflow vs irrelevance is not separated (A06, A07); stakes beyond one simulated shop are asserted (A15).
search_scope: P1 full text incl. Sec 1, 6, Limitations, App A, F
R_REACT Sec 4 WebShop, Table 4, App C.3

M.reason: Operation, information and assumptions reconstructible: stateless summariser sees instruction, previous action and raw page and emits a condensed info[...] with few products/options kept, navigation kept and hints added; stateful actor sees only summarised history (A21, A22). Directly targets the length/irrelevance bottleneck. Not 4: noise-triggers-hallucination is an untested hypothesis (A11); no distinguishable prediction against cheap truncation/top-k alternatives; hint injection means gains are not attributable to pruning alone (A22).
search_scope: P1 Sec 3, App C.1-C.4, D, E

X.reason: Chain fully disclosed: all summariser/actor prompts for both backbones, action space, 20-step cap, invalid-action termination, greedy decoding, environment config and seeds (A18, A19, A21, A22); failure cases shown (A20). Not 4: summariser fidelity/target recall never measured, no gate on bad summaries, in-house ReAct prompt not shown (A17), no transfer boundary tested.

E.measurement.reason: Programmatic WebShop reward (attribute/type/option/price matching; W05), success = score 1.0, two metrics, two backbones; no learned judge. Not 4: comparator is an unvalidated in-house ReAct (A17); abstract 6.2 vs body 6.8 (A01, I04); 500 vs 499 sessions (I02); pilot n inconsistent (I01).
search_scope: P1 Abstract, Sec 4-5, Tables 1-2, App A, F

E.causality.reason: Same-backbone ASH vs ReAct on two models and DIRECT vs DIRECT+ASH support a contribution of the summariser package (A02-A05, A12). Gaps: no ablation of summariser inputs/hints or actor-prompt additions (A22); no rule-based condensation baseline although WebShop simple mode and ReAct-style top-k trimming exist (W04, R04); gpt-3.5 gain confounded with 4k overflow (A06, A07); ASH adds a model call per step; hallucination mechanism is a hypothesis (A11); explicit reasoning still helps (ASH 30.2 > DIRECT+ASH 27.4).
search_scope: P1 Sec 5, Fig 5, App A, C

E.holdout.reason: One simulated shop, text-only, no second environment, unseen site or real browser, while broad applicability is claimed (A15). Backbone chosen on a 50-sample subset of the same 500 (A16). Sessions are random seeds not documented as WebShop's fixed test split (A18, W01, W02, I06), so results are not comparable to published WebShop/ReAct numbers. Narrow WebShop claim is addressed; broad claim has no evidence.
search_scope: P1 Sec 4, Limitations, App A, C, F

E.statistics.reason: Single greedy run per configuration; no seeds, variance, CI or tests, yet 'significant' is used. Partial failure analysis (invalid-action shares A10, A11, two summariser failures A20); share denominators differ across methods (I03); realised-length bins outcome-conditioned (A08, A09); pilot n inconsistent (I01). Not 0 because task count and some failure boundaries are given.
search_scope: Complete P1 incl. Tables 1-2, Figs 4-5, App A-F searched for seeds/repeats/variance/intervals

E.cost.reason: Interface-level parity only: same backbone, greedy decoding, 500 max tokens, 20-step cap and termination rule. resolutions.reason: ASH's central operation is liberating a conventionally fixed component of the iterative action-generation loop (raw observation as the actor's conditioning) and redesigning it into an action-aware condensed intermediate; authors state this framing explicitly ('previous prompting approaches always put the full observation'). This matches the card definition (intermediate representation / conditioning of a staged procedure) and when-to-apply (inherited default never the actual constraint), and the 'frozen pretrained models, no retraining' success condition. decompose_and_delegate's when-to-apply requires delegating part of the task to a sound external/symbolic solver with verifiable artifacts; both ASH stages are the same LLM exchanging free text, and son55 itself rated the fit weak with every C25 step unmet. Protocol: do not match on 'uses multiple modules'. Sub-card null (sol checked C15/C23/C24: diffusion/geometric/refinement tactics do not apply).

Few-shot prompting is the delivery mechanism of every prompt-only method here, not a distinct operation; the paper's claim is not task generalisation by conditioning (no category holdout, no conditioning-channel training). PATTERN_PROTOCOL step 3: supporting only when a different operation needs it.

shared_error_corrections.both_seats: Lineage rested on ASH's own description (sol: unverified -> G unknown; son55: 'described by this paper only').
shared_error_corrections.correction: Verified against shared originals: ReAct (2210.03629v3) treats WebShop observations as noisy and handles them via in-actor reasoning, reporting score 66.6 / SR 40.0 (PaLM) next to WebShop IL/IL+RL; its WebShop exemplars show 3 results per page while WebShop pages hold 10. Authors' 'ReAct is closest' and 'top-3 trimming' statements are consistent with the originals.

shared_error_corrections.both_seats: Both treat '500 tasks' as the evaluation set without checking it against WebShop's standard split.
shared_error_corrections.correction: WebShop defines a fixed 500-instruction i.i.d. test split on which published WebShop and ReAct numbers are reported (W01, W02). ASH samples random session strings from seeds 501..999 (A18, I02) and never states these are the test split; its 'previous state of the art' is the in-house ReAct (23.4 SR) rather than published ReAct (40.0 SR under PaLM/simple mode). The supported comparison is internal to ASH's harness only (I06).
shared_error_corrections.score_impact: none (E.holdout already 1, E.measurement 3); narrows claim wording

shared_error_corrections.both_seats: Both note a missing 'simple truncation / top-k' baseline but neither identifies that WebShop itself ships a rule-based simplified observation mode used by all WebShop models.
shared_error_corrections.correction: WebShop's simple mode strips extraneous HTML metadata (W04) and ReAct-style top-3 trimming (R04) are off-the-shelf rule-based condensers in the same environment, making the missing cheap-condensation control concrete rather than hypothetical.
shared_error_corrections.score_impact: none (supports G not 4 and E.causality=2 as both seats rated)
